origin.description: Calculate nodes and weights for Gaussian quadrature.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Number of nodes and weights. Truncated to an integer. A negative count is an error, and zero returns empty vectors.

arguments.name: kind
arguments.text: Quadrature weight. One of legendre, chebyshev1, chebyshev2, hermite, jacobi, or laguerre. A unique prefix is accepted.

arguments.name: alpha
arguments.text: Parameter for Jacobi or Laguerre quadrature. The manual requires it to be greater than -1.

arguments.name: beta
arguments.text: Second parameter for Jacobi quadrature. The manual requires it to be greater than -1.

origin.details: The integral of w(x) f(x) is approximated by sum(weights * f(nodes)). The approximation is exact when f is a polynomial of degree at most 2n-1. Legendre uses w(x)=1 on (-1,1). Chebyshev of the first kind uses 1/sqrt(1-x^2), and the second kind uses sqrt(1-x^2), both on (-1,1). Hermite uses exp(-x^2) on the whole line. Jacobi uses (1-x)^alpha * (1+x)^beta on (-1,1). Laguerre uses x^alpha * exp(-x) on (0, Inf). The nodes are the eigenvalues of the Jacobi matrix of the orthogonal polynomials, from the Golub-Welsch algorithm.
origin.value: A list with nodes and weights.

translation.example:

print(float(sum(out["weights"] * out["nodes"]) / math.gamma(6)))
